body.statement: For nuisance sequences with \(\eta_{NT}\to\eta\), uniformly over compact subsets of \(\mathcal G_{\mathrm{loc}}\) and every finite \(M\), \(\sup_{|x|\le M}|(\sigma^2T)^{-1}[Q_F(\gamma+\sigma x/\sqrt m)-Q_F(\gamma)]-[\Phi_{NT,h}(x)-\Phi_{NT,h}(0)]|\xrightarrow{p}0\). Moreover, \(\widehat x_F=O_p(1)\) uniformly and \(\operatorname{dist}\{\widehat x_F,\mathcal S_{NT}(h)\}\xrightarrow{p}0\). Here \(h=\theta/\sigma\in[-\overline h,\overline h]\); no stochastic assertion is made for unbounded \(h\) or a genuine limiting tie.
body.justification: This is the bridge from fixed-spike random-matrix theory to the coefficient chosen by the actual full-sample IFE objective on a bounded local experiment.
body.gap: Benaych-Georges and Nadakuditi (2012) give fixed-spike limits; Bai (2009) does not cover a noise-scale treatment factor or uniform coefficient-indexed spectral localization.
body.consumer: It supplies the limit experiment needed to determine whether whole-sample profiling can absorb local low-rank heterogeneity even after ordinary baseline-confounding terms are removed by assumption.
